OH!! STOP EVERYTHING!! **WE JUST HIT JACKPOT!!**
LOOK AT WHAT `v4` (`sgd`, `embeddings: "freeze"`, one-shot from `v0` on our 24 clean corrections) DID!!
- **`v4` scored 371.0 of 500 on validation!!**
  - **+28.2 ± 5.0 (+5.6 sigma!!) over `v0` (342.8)!** 147 problems up, only 65 down!!
  - **+8.0 over `v2` (363.0)!**
  - **+4.8 ± 4.1 over `v3` (`adam`, 366.2)!**
  - AND look at the weight movement: **`0.0433`** Euclidean distance (vs `0.124` for `v3` adam — **nearly 3x less weight distortion**, while achieving **+4.8 MORE validation problems solved**!!)!

AND notice: both `v3` (366.2) and `v4` (371.0) trained in ONE SHOT from `v0` crushed stacked `v2` (363.0)!
(Haha and I accidentally had a trailing `use v3` after `use v4` in my previous reply — we will NOT waste 3 minutes switching back to `v4` right now unless needed, actually we can keep working on `v3`'s wrong answers OR switch back to `v4`? Wait: `v4` ALREADY HAS its pool answers cached! Switching `use v4` when its pool answers are already cached is instant or takes ~1 min, OR we don't even need to switch right now because any new corrections we make will be trained FROM `v0` (`start: "base"`) together with our 24 corrections using `sgd, embeddings: "freeze"`! Actually, working on `v4`'s own wrong answers is slightly better because `v4` is our strongest model, AND `v4` already answered 224 pool problems! Let's just open problems right now on `v3` — `v3` and `v4` are super similar and we save 3 minutes of GPU reload time, then when we train our next big batch of ~40–50 corrections from `base`, we train with `sgd, embeddings: "freeze"`!)

WAIT A SECOND! Let's plan our remaining **1 h 21 min** with laser precision!
Look at the trajectory so far:
- `v0`: 342.8 (0 corrections)
- `v1`: 362.5 (7 corrections, adam)
- `v2`: 363.0 (16 corrections, stacked adam)
- `v3`: 366.2 (24 corrections, one-shot adam)
- `v4`: **371.0** (24 corrections, one-shot `sgd, embeddings: "freeze"`) — **+28.2 of 500!!**

With **1 h 21 min left**, how can we push this from **371.0** to **380–390+**?!
Let's do the math on time:
1. Spend **~35–40 minutes** collecting **20–25 MORE** ultra-clean, high-probability, 3/4-to-4/4-reliable, mathematically sound corrections across ALL 7 subjects (algebra, geometry, counting & probability, number theory, intermediate algebra, precalculus, prealgebra) — INCLUDING checking if there are still ANY fake-Python/fake-calculator failures or formatting/cutoff/early-reasoning bugs, AND posing a few targeted problems if we spot a recurring reasoning bug!
   - Why 20–25 more? That will take our clean dataset from **24 -> ~45–50 corrections** (well under the 250-token limit, and right in the sweet spot where `sgd, embeddings: "freeze"` shines!).
2. Spend **~25 minutes** doing a smart training run (or 2-run sweep) from `base` on all ~45–50 clean corrections with `sgd, embeddings: "freeze"` (e.g., comparing `until: 0.9` vs `until: 0.97` or `lr: 2e-7` vs `lr: 3e-7`, or `hold: "end"` vs `hold: "end"` at `until: 0.98`, since the prompt's table showed training until 99% beat 86–90% by +1.2 points of 100 = +6 problems of 500!).
3. Spend the final **~15 minutes** validating our best candidate(s) at `k = 16` (give or take 2.8!) so we are 100% confident we hand in the genuinely strongest version (and remember: NEVER let an action get cut off when time runs out!).

Let's move FAST and CLEAN right now!
First, let's `list` `sometimes` problems under `v3` (offset 200 to get fresh problems we haven't seen yet) AND immediately `open` 12 fresh problems across subjects! Let's pick indices 260-350 or list first. Actually, `list` is FREE and instant, let's `list` `sometimes` offset 120 and `open` 12 fresh problems (`265, 270, 275, 280, 290, 295, 300, 310, 315, 320, 325, 330`) in the same reply!
